rw: Planning tasks by priority and deadlines is good time management. It makes sure the most important and urgent work gets done first and on time.

ww.Starting many tasks without finishing th: Starting many tasks without finishing them spreads effort thin and leaves nothing completed. Good time management means finishing work, not just beginning it.
ww.Ignoring deadlines set by the manager: Ignoring deadlines set by the manager causes late work and lost trust. Time management means respecting deadlines and planning backward from them.
ww.Doing every task at the last minute: Doing every task at the last minute leaves no time for checking or for surprises. It is procrastination, the opposite of managing time well.

rw: A résumé should list contact details, education, work experience and skills. Together they show an employer who you are and what you can do.

ww.Your bank balance and the amount of mone: A bank balance and savings are private financial details. Employers do not need them, and they have no place on a résumé.
ww.A list of everything you dislike about p: Listing what you dislike about past jobs is negative and unprofessional. A résumé should highlight strengths and achievements instead.
ww.Your passwords for all of your online ac: Passwords are private and must never be shared. Putting them on a résumé would create a serious security risk and does not help your application.

rw: A thank-you message shows appreciation, restates your interest and leaves a good final impression. It is a standard professional courtesy after an interview.

ww.Post complaints about the company online: Posting complaints about the company online looks unprofessional and could end your chance at the job. Employers often search social media.
ww.Call repeatedly each hour until they ans: Calling every hour is pushy and annoying. It suggests poor judgment and will probably hurt rather than help your chances.
ww.Ignore the opportunity and never follow: Ignoring the opportunity and never following up wastes a chance to show interest. A short follow-up keeps you on the employer's mind.

rw: Networking helps you learn about opportunities and get advice. Contacts can share job leads, mentor you and introduce you to useful people.

ww.It replaces the need for skills on the j: Networking cannot replace job skills. Contacts may open doors, but you still need the ability to do the work once you are hired.
ww.It guarantees a promotion within a year: No amount of networking guarantees a promotion in a year. It creates chances and advice, but results depend on performance.
ww.It prevents you from changing jobs at al: Networking does not stop you changing jobs. If anything, it makes moving to a better job easier because more people know you.

rw: Professionalism includes reliability, respect and appropriate appearance. Together they build trust with coworkers, managers and customers.

ww.Arriving late without notice and leaving: Arriving late without notice and leaving early shows a lack of reliability. Professionalism means being punctual and communicating about absences.
ww.Gossiping about coworkers behind their b: Gossiping behind coworkers' backs damages trust and teamwork. Professional people keep conversations respectful and avoid spreading rumors.
ww.Ignoring workplace rules and company pol: Ignoring workplace rules and policies is unprofessional. Following them shows responsibility and keeps the workplace fair and safe.

rw: Building leadership skills through training and experience prepares someone for a manager role. It shows readiness and gives the employee the abilities managers need.

ww.Hide accomplishments from supervisors an: Hiding accomplishments keeps supervisors from seeing your value. Promotion usually depends on visible results, so sharing success is important.
ww.Stop learning new skills and stay in the: Staying in one role and not learning new skills limits growth. Managers need broader knowledge, so continuing to learn matters.
ww.Avoid taking on any new responsibilities: Avoiding new responsibilities leaves you with no chance to show leadership. Taking on more is how people prove they are ready to advance.

rw: Industries and technology change over time, so skills can become outdated. Continuing to learn keeps workers useful and employable throughout a career.

ww.Change never affects any business at all: Change does affect nearly every business, whether through technology, markets or rules. That is why workers need to keep learning.
ww.Training prevents all mistakes at the fi: Training does not prevent all mistakes. It reduces them, but no amount of learning removes every error.
ww.Learning ends once a person has a job: Learning does not end once a person has a job. Workplaces keep changing, so successful people keep building skills for many years.

rw: A threat is an outside factor that could harm the business. A big supermarket adding an in-store bakery may take customers from the small bakery.

ww.Chance: A chance is an opportunity, a favorable outside factor. A new competitor entering your market is an unfavorable outside factor, so it is not a chance.
ww.Strength: A strength is an internal advantage of the business. The supermarket is an outside force, so it cannot be one of the bakery's strengths.
ww.Weakness: A weakness is an internal problem, such as poor equipment. The supermarket's plan comes from outside the bakery, so it is not a weakness.

rw: In controlling, managers compare results with goals and take corrective action when there is a gap. This keeps the organization on track toward its objectives.

ww.Choose employees' lunch times and assign: Choosing lunch times and parking spaces are minor administrative tasks. They are not the core controlling function of comparing results with goals.
ww.Print company brochures for the sales te: Printing brochures is a routine marketing task. It does not involve measuring results against goals.
ww.Set the company's logo and the colors us: Setting a logo and ad colors is a branding decision. Controlling is about monitoring performance and correcting problems.

rw: Risk management is identifying and reducing possible threats to a business. It protects assets, people and profits from avoidable harm.

ww.Taking every risk without thought, hopin: Taking every risk without thought is reckless. Risk management means weighing risks carefully rather than gambling on luck.
ww.Hiding risks from owners and all of the: Hiding risks from owners and managers prevents anyone from preparing. Risk management depends on open sharing of information.
ww.Ignoring risks to save time and money fo: Ignoring risks leaves the business exposed. A problem that could have been prevented may become expensive later.

rw: Buying insurance transfers the financial risk of fire damage to the insurer. The company pays a premium and the insurer covers the loss.

ww.Accepting the risk: Accepting a risk means choosing to bear the loss yourself. Buying insurance does not do that; it hands the cost to an insurer.
ww.Avoiding all risk: Avoiding risk means not doing the risky activity at all. The company still operates, so it is not avoiding the fire risk.
ww.Ignoring risk: Ignoring risk is doing nothing about it. Buying insurance is a deliberate action to deal with the danger.

rw: Increasing online sales by 10 percent within six months is specific, measurable and time-bound. It fits the SMART guideline.

ww.Make more money someday in the near futu: Making more money someday is vague, with no number or date. A SMART goal must be specific and measurable.
ww.Improve a little bit over the coming mon: Improving a little bit over the coming months has no measure or deadline. It cannot be checked, so it is not SMART.
ww.Be the best at everything in the whole i: Being the best at everything in the industry is not realistic or measurable. SMART goals are achievable and specific.

rw: The four functions of management are planning, organizing, leading and controlling. Together they describe how managers set direction and get results.

ww.Saving, spending, lending and then borro: Saving, spending, lending and borrowing are money actions. They are not the functions of management.
ww.Buying, selling, hiring and firing worke: Buying, selling, hiring and firing are business tasks. They are not the four standard functions of management.
ww.Writing, reading, speaking and listening: Writing, reading, speaking and listening are communication skills. They are not the management functions.

rw: Stating in the contract who owns the intellectual property settles the question clearly in writing. It prevents a later dispute over the finished design.

ww.Rely on a verbal comment made at the fir: A verbal comment at a meeting is hard to prove later. Ownership should be written in the contract.
ww.Assume the freelancer keeps all ownershi: Assuming the freelancer keeps ownership by default is risky. Rules vary, so the parties should state the agreement in writing.
ww.Wait until the app is finished and then: Waiting until the app is finished to decide ownership invites conflict. Both sides will have a stake in the result, so decide beforehand.

rw: An NDA protects confidential business information from being shared. The people who sign agree not to reveal secrets such as plans or customer lists.

ww.An employee's right to a raise in pay ea: A raise in pay is a compensation matter. An NDA concerns keeping information private, not an employee's earnings.
ww.A building from fire damage and other ha: Protection from fire damage comes from insurance. An NDA is a legal agreement about secrecy.
ww.A product from being sold overseas, as e: Controls on selling products overseas are export rules. An NDA does not deal with exports.

rw: Turning a free trial into a paid subscription without a clear warning is a deceptive or unfair practice. Consumer protection law requires clear disclosure.

ww.Import licensing rules for foreign goods: Import licensing concerns bringing foreign goods into a country. A hidden paid subscription is a consumer protection matter.
ww.Zoning restrictions on where a shop may: Zoning rules control where a shop may be located. They have nothing to do with hidden subscription charges.
ww.Overtime violations, such as unpaid hour: Overtime violations involve unpaid extra hours for employees. The scenario concerns customers, not workers.

rw: Collecting and paying sales tax is required by law, and not doing so brings penalties. Fines or legal action can follow errors.

ww.It is optional for small shops with very: Sales tax is not optional for small shops. Businesses must collect and send it whatever their size, depending on local rules.
ww.It increases the store's profit margin a: Sales tax is collected from customers and passed on, so it does not add to profit. Keeping it would be illegal.
ww.It replaces income tax entirely for the: Sales tax does not replace income tax. A business may owe both, since they are separate taxes.

rw: Defamation is making false statements that damage someone's reputation. Posting false claims about a competitor can lead to a lawsuit.

ww.Trademark: A trademark protects a brand name or logo. It does not cover false statements about a rival.
ww.Zoning: Zoning concerns where and how land can be used. It is unrelated to damaging a competitor's reputation.
ww.Bankruptcy: Bankruptcy is a legal process for debts. It is not the issue when someone posts false claims.

rw: Workplace safety regulations protect employees from hazards and injury. They set standards for equipment, training and conditions.

ww.To control product prices in all of the: Controlling product prices is not the purpose of safety rules. Safety regulations focus on protecting workers.
ww.To restrict which customers may shop the: Safety rules do not decide which customers may shop. They deal with conditions for employees.
ww.To limit how much employees may earn a y: Limiting what employees earn is a wage matter. Safety regulations are about preventing harm.

rw: Bankruptcy lets a person or business seek legal relief from debts they cannot pay. A court oversees the process, which can cancel or reorganize some debts.

ww.Avoid all future taxes, so none are paid: Bankruptcy does not erase future taxes. It deals with existing debts, and taxes still apply afterwards.
ww.Ignore all contracts that the person has: Bankruptcy does not let someone ignore contracts. It is a legal process, with rules for how debts are handled.
ww.Borrow without limits from any lender at: Bankruptcy does not give unlimited borrowing. A bankruptcy record usually makes borrowing harder.

rw: Refusing to rent because of religion is unlawful discrimination. Anti-discrimination laws protect people from unfair treatment based on religion.

ww.A lawful marketing move: Turning someone away for religion is not marketing. It is unequal treatment that the law forbids.
ww.A normal pricing decision: A pricing decision is about charging a fee. Refusing service for religion is discrimination, not pricing.
ww.A required zoning rule: A zoning rule controls land use. It does not allow a landlord to refuse a tenant for religion.

rw: Consideration is something of value exchanged by each party. It can be money, goods, services or a promise, and it makes a contract binding.

ww.A polite thank-you note after signing: A thank-you note is a courtesy. Consideration is value exchanged in a contract.
ww.A discount offered after a complaint is: A discount after a complaint is a customer service gesture. It is not consideration in the contract sense.
ww.A background check on all of the signers: A background check is a screening step. It is not consideration.

rw: Explaining the reasons honestly and respectfully, and allowing questions, treats employees as adults. It keeps trust even when the news is bad.

ww.Hide the reason and say nothing to the s: Hiding the reason and saying nothing breeds rumors and distrust. Employees should hear the news from the manager directly.
ww.Blame another department in public for a: Blaming another department in public is unfair and divisive. It harms morale and avoids responsibility.
ww.Announce it by anonymous note and leave: An anonymous note and leaving before questions is cowardly and disrespectful. Employees deserve a chance to ask.

rw: An agenda lists topics and keeps the discussion on track. Everyone knows what will be covered and can prepare in advance.

ww.To prove the meeting was held on the rig: An agenda does not prove a meeting date. Its job is to plan the topics and keep discussion focused.
ww.To record each person's salary and job t: Salaries and job titles are HR records. They do not belong on a meeting agenda.
ww.To list items to buy for the office this: A shopping list for the office is not an agenda. Agendas list meeting topics.

rw: Plain language and checking for understanding help the customer follow the policy. The rep can ask questions to confirm they understood.

ww.Read the policy aloud with no examples g: Reading the policy aloud with no examples does not help a confused customer. The policy is hard to follow, so it needs explaining.
ww.Speak much faster so the call ends soone: Speaking faster makes confusion worse. A confused customer needs a slower, clearer explanation.
ww.Use technical terms to show your experti: Technical terms to show expertise add to confusion. The goal is to be understood, not to impress.

rw: A business letter with a résumé is the standard format for a formal application. It is professional and gives the employer what they need.

ww.A voicemail with no job details: A voicemail with no job details gives the employer nothing to consider. A formal application should be written and clear.
ww.A text message full of emojis: A text full of emojis is too casual for a formal application. It would look unprofessional.
ww.A short social media post online: A short social media post is not a formal application. Employers expect a proper document.

rw: A language barrier occurs when words or slang are not understood by the listener. Unfamiliar slang is a common example.

ww.A distance barrier: A distance barrier involves physical space between people. The problem here was the words used.
ww.A time-zone barrier: A time-zone barrier arises when people work in different time zones. It does not describe confusion over slang.
ww.A hardware barrier: A hardware barrier concerns equipment failure. The misunderstanding came from language, not machines.

rw: Proofreading catches errors that could hurt credibility. A clean message shows care and professionalism.

ww.It makes a message longer than it needs: Proofreading does not aim to make a message longer. It checks for mistakes.
ww.It guarantees a reply from the reader ri: Proofreading cannot guarantee a reply. Replies depend on the reader.
ww.It removes the need for a clear purpose: Proofreading does not remove the need for a purpose. A message still needs a clear aim.

rw: Constructive criticism is specific, respectful and focused on improvement. It tells the person what to do better and treats them with respect.

ww.Speak in vague general terms about the w: Vague, general comments do not help someone improve. People need to know what to change.
ww.Focus only on personal traits rather tha: Focusing on personal traits is unfair and hurtful. Criticism should address the work, not the person.
ww.Criticize in front of the team so all le: Criticizing in front of the team humiliates the person. Constructive feedback is usually given in private.

rw: Offering the exchange, explaining the policy and escalating for a possible exception respects the rules and tries to help the customer. It may win a refund with approval.

ww.Give a refund without checking policy, s: Giving a refund without checking policy ignores company rules. The customer is important, but staff should follow procedures.
ww.Refuse and end the conversation right aw: Refusing and ending the conversation leaves a customer with a broken item and no help. It damages the relationship.
ww.Say the customer surely must have broken: Accusing the customer of breaking it is rude and unfair. It assumes the worst without evidence.

rw: Reducing waiting and responding promptly shows respect for customers' time. It makes service quicker and more pleasant.

ww.Add more steps to every purchase: Adding steps to every purchase wastes customers' time. It shows the business does not value it.
ww.Delay replies to emails from customers: Delaying replies to emails frustrates customers. Prompt replies show respect for their time.
ww.Close the checkout lanes at busy times: Closing checkout lanes at busy times creates long lines. That wastes customers' time.

rw: Staying calm, acknowledging the frustration and focusing on a solution keeps the call professional. The caller feels heard and the problem can move forward.

ww.Match the caller's anger and raise your: Matching the caller's anger and raising your voice escalates the conflict. It makes a professional resolution much harder.
ww.Argue about who is correct so the caller: Arguing about who is correct wastes time and increases tension. The goal is to solve the problem.
ww.Hang up immediately without helping the: Hanging up without helping abandons the customer. It would anger them further and harm the company.

rw: Going the extra mile means doing more than the customer expects. It builds loyalty and delight.

ww.Promise things you cannot deliver: Promising things you cannot deliver sets up disappointment. Going the extra mile means delivering real value.
ww.Avoid helping customers in the store: Avoiding helping customers is the opposite of going the extra mile. It shows no effort.
ww.Do only what the policy requires: Doing only what policy requires is the minimum. The extra mile means going beyond it.

rw: Employees need to know company policies so they can explain them accurately to customers. This avoids confusion and mistakes.

ww.So they can change them freely at any ti: Employees cannot change policies freely. Policies are set by management.
ww.So they can hide them from customers who: Hiding policies from customers is dishonest. Customers should be told the rules.
ww.So they can ignore them when they are bu: Ignoring policies when busy leads to inconsistent service and errors. Staff should follow policy at all times.

rw: Studying the checkout process and finding ways to speed it up responds directly to the feedback. It improves the customer experience.

ww.Blame the customers for being so impatie: Blaming customers for impatience does not solve the problem. It makes the business look defensive.
ww.Ignore the survey results and change not: Ignoring survey results wastes useful feedback. The business asked, so it should act on the answers.
ww.Make the checkout longer so it looks car: Making checkout longer makes the complaint worse. Customers already dislike the delay.

rw: Keeping promises about price, quality and delivery builds trust. Customers learn they can rely on the business.

ww.Hiding fees from customers until the tim: Hiding fees until payment is deceptive. It destroys trust.
ww.Changing prices without notice on each v: Changing prices without notice makes customers feel cheated. It erodes trust.
ww.Ignoring customer questions about the pr: Ignoring questions about the product leaves customers unsure. It shows poor service.

rw: A complaint is a chance to learn and improve the product or service. It shows what customers care about and what to fix.

ww.Prove the customer wrong in front of oth: Proving the customer wrong in front of others shames them. A complaint is not a contest.
ww.Avoid the customer so they stop complain: Avoiding the customer leaves the problem unsolved. It does not make the complaint go away.
ww.Lower the quality of service to save mon: Lowering service quality to save money makes problems worse. Complaints should lead to improvement.

rw: When wheat supply falls, wheat becomes scarcer and costlier. Bread prices tend to rise because bakers pay more.

ww.It will not change: A drought reduces wheat supply, so costs rise. Bread prices would not stay unchanged.
ww.It will tend to fall: Prices tend to fall when supply rises. A drought reduces supply, so the effect is the opposite.
ww.It will become zero: Bread would not become free. Scarcer wheat raises costs, so prices go up.

rw: A trade deficit means imports exceed exports. The country buys more from abroad than it sells.

ww.Exports exceed imports: When exports exceed imports, a country has a trade surplus. That is the opposite of a deficit.
ww.Taxes exceed spending: Taxes exceeding spending is a budget surplus. It is not about trade.
ww.Prices fall in the economy: Falling prices describe deflation. A trade deficit is about imports and exports.

rw: A factory polluting a river harms nearby towns who did not choose it. That is a negative externality, a cost imposed on others.

ww.A shop sells goods at a profit to local: A shop selling goods at a profit to local people is an ordinary transaction. No outside party bears a cost.
ww.A bakery's smell attracts customers who: A bakery's smell attracting customers is a positive externality for neighbors. It benefits others without payment.
ww.A school raises its tuition fees every y: A school raising tuition affects the people who pay it. It is not a cost imposed on outsiders.

rw: The unemployment rate measures the share of the labor force that is jobless and looking for work. It shows how many people cannot find jobs.

ww.The share of older people who retire fro: The share of older people who retire is a retirement rate. The unemployment rate counts jobless people who want work.
ww.The share of firms that fail each year i: Firms failing each year is a business failure rate. It is not the unemployment rate.
ww.The share of workers who earn the minimu: Workers earning the minimum wage is a wage statistic. It does not measure unemployment.

rw: Subsidies encourage certain activities by lowering costs for producers. Governments use them to support industries such as farming and clean energy.

ww.To collect more taxes from firms and fro: Subsidies give money to producers. They do not collect more taxes from firms.
ww.To prohibit business activity in sectors: Subsidies do not prohibit business activity. They support it.
ww.To raise prices on all goods sold in the: Subsidies lower costs and prices. They do not raise prices on all goods.

rw: A free enterprise system is an economy where private owners run businesses for profit. Competition and consumer choice guide what is produced.

ww.An economy with no money used for any ki: Money is used in free enterprise. An economy with no money would rely on barter.
ww.An economy where the government owns all: Government ownership of everything is a command economy. Free enterprise relies on private owners.
ww.An economy without any competition betwe: Free enterprise has competition between private firms. It does not remove competition.

rw: Calmly speaking with the teammate privately is mature. It lets you clear up the issue without public conflict.

ww.Embarrass the teammate in a meeting so a: Embarrassing the teammate in a meeting is immature and escalates conflict. It does not address the problem constructively.
ww.Spread rumors about the teammate to the: Spreading rumors is unprofessional and damages relationships. It harms your reputation as well.
ww.Refuse to work with anyone on the team a: Refusing to work with anyone ever again overreacts. It harms the team and your own career.

rw: Being adaptable means adjusting to new situations and changes. Adaptable people stay flexible when plans shift.

ww.Refusing to try any new methods at work: Refusing new methods is the opposite of adaptable. It shows inflexibility.
ww.Complaining whenever the plans change: Complaining whenever plans change shows resistance. Adaptable people cope with change.
ww.Avoiding all change at the workplace: Avoiding all change is not adaptable. Adaptable employees embrace it.

rw: Teamwork combines skills, which helps solve problems and reach goals. People with different strengths cover for each other.

ww.It removes the need for leaders in the w: Teamwork does not remove the need for leaders. Teams still need direction.
ww.It makes work slower in every case, as p: Teamwork does not slow work in every case. Good teams often finish faster.
ww.It ensures nobody ever makes any mistake: Teamwork cannot ensure nobody makes mistakes. It helps catch them.

rw: Apologizing after snapping shows accountability and respect for others. It repairs trust and sets a good example.

ww.Weak leadership that should be hidden: Weak leadership is not what an apology shows. Apologizing is a sign of strength.
ww.A way to avoid all feedback at work: An apology does not avoid feedback. It accepts responsibility.
ww.A need to avoid the employee for a while: Avoiding the employee does not fix the harm. An apology does.

rw: Integrity means doing the right thing even when no one is watching. It shows honest, consistent character.

ww.Hiding mistakes from the boss and from t: Hiding mistakes is the opposite of integrity. Integrity means honesty.
ww.Doing whatever is easiest for you at the: Doing whatever is easiest is convenience. Integrity means choosing what is right.
ww.Following rules only when observed by a: Following rules only when observed is not integrity. It depends on being watched.

rw: Listening without interrupting respects coworkers' ideas. It tells them you value what they say.

ww.Interrupting to share an idea: Interrupting to share your idea cuts others off. It shows poor respect for their ideas.
ww.Dismissing ideas without thought: Dismissing ideas without thought shows disrespect. Everyone's ideas deserve a fair hearing.
ww.Laughing at unusual suggestions: Laughing at unusual suggestions mocks the person. It discourages sharing.

rw: Asking what help they need and offering support shows empathy and teamwork. It lightens the load and builds trust.

ww.Take credit for their work and say nothi: Taking credit for their work is dishonest and harms them. It shows no empathy.
ww.Tell them to work harder and stop compla: Telling them to work harder dismisses their struggle. It shows no care.
ww.Report them to the manager without speak: Reporting them without speaking to them first is unfair. A kind talk should come first.

rw: Conflict resolution means finding a fair solution to a disagreement. It lets people move forward and keeps relationships healthy.

ww.Avoiding all discussion of the problem: Avoiding all discussion leaves the problem unresolved. It tends to grow.
ww.Winning an argument at any cost to be ri: Winning an argument at any cost is not resolution. It leaves the other side resentful.
ww.Punishing everyone involved in the dispu: Punishing everyone does not solve the dispute. It creates more conflict.

rw: A part-time worker or freelancer gives help at lower cost. The founder pays only for the work needed.

ww.Close the whole business for good now: Closing the business is an extreme response to a hiring problem. It does not control costs while getting help.
ww.Hire five full-time workers right away: Hiring five full-time workers adds big costs the founder cannot afford. It does not match the budget.
ww.Do nothing and let the work pile up: Doing nothing lets work pile up and hurts the business. It does not solve the problem.

rw: A start-up cost is an expense needed to launch a business. Examples are equipment, licenses, deposits and initial stock.

ww.A tax refund from the state for the firm: A tax refund is money returned to a taxpayer. A start-up cost is an expense to launch.
ww.A profit from the first sale of goods: A profit from the first sale comes after launch. Start-up costs come before.
ww.A discount for loyal customers each mont: A loyalty discount is a marketing reward. It is not a start-up cost.

rw: A USP describes what makes a product different from competitors. It gives customers a reason to choose it.

ww.The location of the store and its openin: Store location and hours are practical details. They are not a USP.
ww.A discount on all items sold at the stor: A discount is a short-term promotion. It does not describe what makes a product unique.
ww.The cost to produce a product, including: The cost to produce is a financial figure. It is not a USP.

rw: A small pop-up stand or market booth tests demand at low cost. It lets the owner learn what customers want before investing more.

ww.Buy new equipment for ten locations: Buying equipment for ten locations spends large sums before demand is known. It is risky for someone with few savings.
ww.Hire a large staff before selling anythi: Hiring a large staff before selling anything adds costs without proof. It is risky.
ww.Sign a long expensive lease immediately: Signing a long expensive lease commits money before demand is known. It is risky.

rw: An LLC is a business form that protects owners' personal assets. Owners are usually not personally liable for business debts.

ww.A business that cannot ever earn any pro: An LLC is able to earn profit. It is a legal form for a business.
ww.A business owned by the government, run: A business owned by the government is a public enterprise. An LLC is private.
ww.A business with no owners and no legal f: An LLC is a legal form with owners called members. It does have owners.

rw: Record keeping tracks income and expenses and supports tax filing. It shows how the business is doing and helps with decisions.

ww.It hides money from lenders to qualify f: Hiding money from lenders is dishonest. Good records should be accurate.
ww.It prevents all competition from other s: Records cannot prevent competition. They help manage the business.
ww.It makes customers buy more from the who: Record keeping does not make customers buy more. It supports management.

rw: Planning resources, staffing and cash flow before accepting more prevents overload. It lets the business grow without failing.

ww.Promise quick delivery with no plan to w: Promising quick delivery with no plan risks failing the customer. Growth needs planning.
ww.Ignore deadlines and hope that things al: Ignoring deadlines and hoping risks missing them. The contract may be lost.
ww.Cancel all other customers to focus on t: Cancelling other customers loses stable business. It puts all her income in one contract.

rw: Profit margin is net income divided by sales. $12,000 divided by $120,000 is 0.10, or 10%.

ww.1%: 1% would need net income of $1,200 on $120,000 of sales. The actual figure is higher.
ww.100%: 100% would mean all sales were profit. Net income is only part of sales.
ww.12%: 12% takes the 12,000 as a percentage. The margin is $12,000 divided by $120,000, which is 10%.

rw: A liability is an amount a business owes to others. Examples are loans and accounts payable.

ww.Money received from customers for sales: Money received from customers for sales is revenue. A liability is something owed.
ww.Something a business owns and can use: Something a business owns and can use is an asset. A liability is the opposite.
ww.Profit left over after all taxes: Profit left over after taxes is net income. A liability is a debt.

rw: The purpose of savings is to set money aside for future needs or goals. It prepares for emergencies and planned purchases.

ww.To avoid earning interest, as cash is sa: Savings do earn interest, usually. Avoiding interest is not the purpose.
ww.To raise debt so the person owes more la: Raising debt is borrowing. Savings are set aside, not borrowed.
ww.To spend more today than the person earn: Spending more than you earn leads to debt. Savings help avoid it.

rw: Spending $3,300 on $3,000 of income leaves a gap of $300 a month. The person must borrow or use savings.

ww.A guaranteed pay raise: A pay raise is decided by the employer. Spending more does not earn one.
ww.A growing savings balance: Savings grow when income exceeds spending. Here spending exceeds income.
ww.No effect on finances: Spending more than income affects finances. It leads to debt or lower savings.

rw: APR stands for annual percentage rate. It shows the yearly cost of borrowing, including interest and some fees.

ww.Average payment record: Average payment record is not what APR stands for. APR is a standard lending term.
ww.Annual profit ratio: Annual profit ratio is not the meaning. APR relates to loans, not profit.
ww.Account payment reserve: Account payment reserve is not the meaning. APR is annual percentage rate.

rw: A lower rate reduces the total cost of borrowing. Comparing rates helps you choose the cheaper loan.

ww.Loans have no costs at all for the borro: Loans do have costs, mostly interest and fees. Comparing rates shows which loan costs less.
ww.Rates have no effect on the cost of a lo: Rates directly affect the cost of a loan. A higher rate means paying more.
ww.A higher rate always means better servic: A higher rate does not mean better service. It means higher cost.

rw: Putting all savings into one stock exposes her to a lack of diversification. If that company fails, she could lose everything.

ww.Too many different assets: Having too many different assets is diversification, which reduces risk. She has the opposite situation.
ww.Interest-free borrowing: Interest-free borrowing is not a risk of her situation. She is investing, not borrowing.
ww.Excess cash on hand at home: Excess cash at home is not her problem. She put money into one stock.

rw: Gross pay is total earnings before deductions. Taxes and other deductions are taken out afterward.

ww.Pay left over after all taxes: Pay left after taxes is net pay. Gross pay is before deductions.
ww.Benefits paid by the employer: Employer benefits are separate from pay. Gross pay is the paycheck total before deductions.
ww.A bonus paid only once a year: A bonus paid once a year is only part of earnings. Gross pay includes all earnings.

rw: When customers pay slowly while bills are due, cash runs short even with high sales. Sales on credit are not cash yet.

ww.Expenses are never paid by the firm at a: Expenses are paid by firms. Not paying them is not the cause here.

rw: Advertising openings through many channels and communities reaches a wide pool of applicants. It helps attract people from many backgrounds.

ww.Hire only through personal referrals fro: Hiring only through referrals from current staff tends to repeat the same backgrounds. It limits variety.

rw: Background checks verify information and reduce hiring risks. They confirm details such as work history or criminal records.

ww.To lower employee pay and cut the wage b: Background checks do not cut wages. They check candidates.

rw: Discussing the problem and setting clear expectations is the fair first step. It gives the employee a chance to improve.

ww.A customer discount given at the cash re: A customer discount is a sales offer. It is not an employee benefit.

ww.Compression: Compression shrinks files. It is not a scam.

rw: A firewall blocks unauthorized access to a network. It filters traffic to keep out attackers.

ww.Setting a price ceiling to keep food cos: A price ceiling is a legal limit on prices. It does not describe shelf placement.
ww.Hiring more cashiers to work the registe: Hiring cashiers is a staffing decision. It is unrelated to shelf height.

rw: Word-of-mouth marketing is customers telling others about a business. Personal recommendations are trusted and cost little.

ww.Paid TV commercials bought each evening: TV commercials are paid advertising. Word of mouth is free and personal.
ww.A paid billboard on a busy highway nearb: A billboard is paid advertising. Word of mouth comes from customers.
ww.A coupon sent in the mail to your home: A coupon in the mail is direct marketing. It is not word of mouth.

rw: A loss leader is a product sold at a low price to attract customers. The store hopes they buy other items too.

ww.A product sold only to employees at a de: A product sold only to employees is an employee perk. A loss leader aims at customers.
ww.A product that cannot be sold in any sto: A product that cannot be sold anywhere is not a loss leader. Loss leaders are sold.
ww.A product that is always given away for: A product always given away is a freebie. A loss leader is sold, usually at a loss.

rw: Using the same message and look across TV, social media and stores is integrated marketing communications. It makes the brand consistent.

ww.Backward integration of supplies: Backward integration is owning suppliers. It is not about advertising.
ww.Market segmentation for the firm: Market segmentation is dividing customers into groups. The company uses one message everywhere.
ww.Price skimming strategy for a launch: Price skimming is a pricing tactic. It does not describe consistent advertising.

rw: A product's life cycle describes the stages from introduction to decline. The stages are introduction, growth, maturity and decline.

ww.The time it takes to make an item in the: The time to make an item is production time. A life cycle covers a product's time on the market.
ww.The length of a product warranty period: A warranty period is a length of coverage. It is not a life cycle.
ww.The number of units held in stock at the: Units held in stock are inventory. A life cycle is about stages.

rw: Tracking what is wasted and adjusting orders and portions targets the cause. The restaurant buys and serves only what it needs.

ww.Order more of every item to be safe from: Ordering more of every item adds waste. It makes spoilage worse.
ww.Stop tracking inventory and just guess w: Stopping tracking removes information. The restaurant would waste more.
ww.Ignore customer preferences and use what: Ignoring customer preferences leads to unsold food. It increases waste.

rw: Just-in-time inventory means receiving goods only as they are needed. It cuts storage costs and waste.

ww.Keeping large stocks for many years: Keeping large stocks for years is the opposite of JIT. JIT keeps inventory low.
ww.Ordering everything at the start of the: Ordering everything at the start of the year builds a big stock. JIT orders as needed.
ww.Producing nothing at all for the market: Producing nothing is not JIT. JIT produces to match demand.

rw: Streamlining processes removes waste while keeping quality. It lowers costs sensibly.

ww.Use cheaper, unsafe materials today: Cheaper, unsafe materials lower quality and risk harm. They would not be sensible.
ww.Cut all training for the new staff: Cutting training raises errors and hurts quality. It is not a sensible way to cut costs.
ww.Skip safety inspections to save time: Skipping safety inspections risks accidents and fines. It is a poor choice.

rw: An emergency evacuation plan sets out steps for safely leaving a building during danger. It protects people in a fire or other emergency.

ww.A sales target for the next quarter of t: A sales target is a business goal. An evacuation plan is a safety procedure.
ww.A list of employee birthdays posted in t: A list of birthdays is a staff note. It is not a safety plan.
ww.A parking schedule for staff cars and vi: A parking schedule organizes cars. It is not an evacuation plan.

rw: Leading a short project builds leadership skills and shows initiative. It helps the employee grow and be noticed.

ww.It removes accountability from the whole: Leading a project does not remove accountability. It adds responsibility.
ww.It lets you avoid other tasks for a long: Leading does not let you avoid other tasks. It may add work.
ww.It guarantees a big raise by the end of: A raise is not guaranteed. Leadership experience can help in time.

rw: Becoming a department manager within ten years is a long-term career goal. It sets a target position and a timeline.

ww.Finishing today's task before the shift: Finishing today's task is a daily goal. A long-term goal looks years ahead.
ww.Eating lunch on time every day this week: Eating lunch on time is a daily habit. It is not a career goal.
ww.Replying to one email from a client toda: Replying to one email is a short task. It is not long term.

rw: Following the chain of command keeps communication and decisions organized. People know who to report to and who decides.

ww.It prevents employees from speaking at w: It does not stop employees speaking. It guides who they speak to.
ww.It removes accountability from the manag: It does not remove accountability. It clarifies it.
ww.It lets you skip supervisors whenever yo: Skipping supervisors breaks the structure. It causes confusion.

rw: Describing the situation, your action and the result shows how you solve problems. It gives a clear, concrete example.

ww.Give a vague answer with no real details: A vague answer with no details tells the interviewer nothing. It fails to show skill.
ww.Blame a former employer for how you left: Blaming a former employer sounds negative. It hurts your chances.
ww.Say you have never had a problem at any: Saying you have never had a problem is unlikely to be believed. It avoids the question.

rw: A professional portfolio is a collection of work samples showing skills. Employers can see real examples of what you can do.

ww.A list of friends and their phone number: A list of friends is personal. A portfolio shows professional work.
ww.A schedule of vacation days for the staf: A vacation schedule is an HR record. It is not a portfolio.
ww.A collection of receipts from past purch: A collection of receipts is financial records. It is not a portfolio.

rw: Investing more in its online presence follows the growth trend. It puts resources where sales are rising.

ww.Raise store prices and ignore it: Raising store prices and ignoring the trend wastes the signal. It could hurt sales.
ww.Close the website for good soon: Closing the website would end the fastest-growing channel. It is illogical.
ww.Ignore the data and keep things as is: Ignoring the data misses a clear trend. Strategy should respond to evidence.

rw: Comparing costs, benefits and risks of each plan allows an informed choice. It helps managers pick the better expansion.

ww.Flip a coin and follow whatever the resu: Flipping a coin leaves a major decision to chance. Managers should use analysis.
ww.Wait for a competitor to decide for the: Waiting for a competitor to decide gives away control. The firm should decide itself.
ww.Choose the first idea with no analysis a: Choosing the first idea with no analysis is risky. Better options may exist.

rw: Delegation means assigning tasks and authority to others. It frees managers and develops employees.

ww.Firing everyone on the team at once: Firing everyone is not delegation. Delegation shares work.
ww.Refusing to share information with the t: Refusing to share information blocks delegation. It prevents work.
ww.Doing every task alone with no help: Doing every task alone is the opposite of delegation. It overloads one person.

rw: Noticing a problem and starting to fix it without being asked shows initiative. It shows responsibility and drive.

ww.Letting others handle everything while y: Letting others handle everything shows no initiative. It is passive.
ww.Waiting to be told every step of the wor: Waiting to be told every step shows no initiative. It depends on others.
ww.Ignoring problems that are not yours to: Ignoring problems that are not yours avoids initiative. Initiative acts.

rw: Privately and kindly pointing out the pattern lets the person improve without embarrassment. It is respectful and helpful.

ww.Interrupt them back every time they inte: Interrupting them back escalates the issue. It is rude.
ww.Stop attending meetings so you never hea: Avoiding meetings avoids the problem. It does not help the team.
ww.Mock the person publicly in front of the: Mocking the person publicly is cruel. It would harm trust.

rw: Being accountable means accepting responsibility for your actions and results. It includes admitting mistakes and fixing them.

ww.Doing only what is easy and skipping the: Doing only what is easy avoids responsibility. It is not accountability.
ww.Hiding mistakes from the boss so no one: Hiding mistakes avoids responsibility. Accountable people own up.
ww.Blaming others when things go wrong to s: Blaming others avoids responsibility. Accountability means owning results.

rw: Praise raises motivation and builds a stronger team culture. People feel valued and want to keep performing.

ww.Lower morale for the team as others feel: Public praise does not lower morale as a rule. It tends to raise it.
ww.Reduced trust in the supervisor over tim: Praise does not reduce trust. It builds it.
ww.More conflict in every case within the t: Praise does not cause more conflict in every case. It usually encourages cooperation.

rw: A personal bias is a tendency to favor or judge based on preconceived ideas. It can lead to unfair decisions.

ww.A company policy on dress and conduct fo: A dress policy is a company rule. A personal bias is an individual tendency.
ww.A required skill listed in every job adv: A required skill is a job requirement. It is not a bias.
ww.A fact proven by research about every pe: A proven fact is not a bias. Bias is not based on evidence.

rw: A growth mindset believes skills improve with effort and learning. It leads to persistence and progress.

ww.Talent cannot change no matter what you: Believing talent cannot change is a fixed mindset. A growth mindset believes people can improve.
ww.Feedback should be avoided at all times: Avoiding feedback blocks growth. A growth mindset welcomes it.
ww.Mistakes mean failure forever for you: Believing mistakes mean permanent failure is a fixed mindset. Growth mindset sees them as lessons.

rw: Discussing expectations clearly and respecting differences while meeting company standards works for both. It builds understanding and keeps the workplace fair.

ww.Punish only one of the coworkers and ign: Punishing only one coworker is unfair. It ignores the cultural difference.
ww.Assume one culture is wrong and tell tha: Assuming one culture is wrong is disrespectful. It creates resentment.
ww.Ignore the difference completely and let: Ignoring the difference and letting them sort it out leaves the conflict. A manager should guide.

rw: Discussing views respectfully and looking for common ground resolves disagreement. It keeps the team working together.

ww.Avoid speaking to each other for the who: Avoiding each other does not solve disagreement. It leaves tension.
ww.Insult those who disagree with you in te: Insulting people harms relationships. It makes teamwork worse.
ww.Always let the loudest person win to fin: Letting the loudest person win ignores good ideas. It is unfair.

rw: Bootstrapping means starting with personal savings and small revenue instead of outside funding. The owner keeps control and avoids debt.

ww.Sell shares to the public immediately to: Selling shares to the public is raising outside funds. Bootstrapping avoids that.
ww.Borrow from many large banks first befor: Borrowing from many banks is debt financing. Bootstrapping uses your own money.
ww.Receive a government grant in every case: A government grant is outside funding. Bootstrapping relies on yourself.
